title: Key difference: Working code triggers lid via callback, current via useEffect
description: WORKING (commit 830709): internalSetLidOpen() callback triggers animation only on user click. CURRENT: useEffect([lidOpen, actions]) triggers on mount AND on lidOpen changes. Solution: Skip animation on first render OR use callback pattern like working code.

title: Approach 1: Add hasMounted ref to skip lid animation on first render
description: Add const hasMountedRef = useRef(false). In lid useEffect, check if (!hasMountedRef.current) { hasMountedRef.current = true; return; }. This prevents the lid animation from playing on first render.

title: Approach 2: Use previous lidOpen value to detect actual changes
description: Add const prevLidOpenRef = useRef(lidOpen). In lid useEffect, check if (prevLidOpenRef.current === lidOpen) return; else prevLidOpenRef.current = lidOpen. This only animates when lidOpen actually changes, not on mount.

title: Approach 3: Store initialized action in ref, re-init only when actions.rocker changes
description: Use rockerActionRef = useRef(null). In useEffect, check if actions.rocker !== rockerActionRef.current, then initialize and store. In useFrame, use rockerActionRef.current instead of actions.rocker. This handles actions object instability.

title: Rename prevRockerActionRef to rockerActionRef (repurpose debug ref)

title: Update useFrame to use rockerActionRef.current instead of actions.rocker
description: In useFrame, change: const rockerAction = actions.rocker; to: const rockerAction = rockerActionRef.current; This ensures useFrame always uses the initialized action, not a new unstable reference.

title: Update init useEffect: re-init when actions.rocker identity changes
description: Modify the guard logic: instead of just checking rockerInitializedRef, also check if actions.rocker !== rockerActionRef.current. If identity changed, re-initialize and update the ref. This handles hot-reload and edge cases.
